slides.title: Read the package and follow its current view
slides.say: The implementation is ready for isolated behavior review. Source contents, the page on screen, and narration have separate evidence. Package follow-ups use the existing capture approval and message delivery flow.

blocks.lead: Source, current view and narration stay separate.

points: Every member has an inventory and capability state.
Unread and unsupported content remains visible.
A follow-up becomes a draft for the proven sender.

slides.title: The current tab follows manual navigation
slides.say: This is the built frontend running against an isolated backend. The current-view tool reported Delivery after manual navigation. It also read selected text and an expanded detail on the Costs tab.

blocks.alt: The isolated JARVIS package frame showing the Delivery tab.
blocks.caption: An actual browser test artifact. Hidden frames are unavailable as the current view.

slides.title: Inspect pixels before describing a diagram
slides.say: The diagram image came through the real MCP image result. Its arrow runs from Budget to Operations. The supplied caption says the opposite. The result is labeled a reconstructed render of source bytes.

blocks.alt: A source diagram with an arrow from Budget to Operations.
blocks.caption: Source render. It does not establish what is on the Mac display.

slides.title: Follow-ups use the existing approval flow
slides.say: A direct request can prepare a source-grounded message for the proven sender or an explicitly named recipient. The capture shows the wording and source references. Changes to the text, recipient or evidence require another approval.

points: Package content cannot supply a user action scope.
Preparation does not send the message.
The existing message record holds queued, sent and reply status.

slides.title: Review the runtime limits before release
slides.say: The isolated browser run used actual frontend and MCP results with the cloud brain and speech disabled. Remote display capture remains unavailable. Cloud classification latency, spoken read-back and delivery to a real agent still need normal-runtime review before release.

points: Dynamic states and unavailable readers remain gaps.
The implementation map and raw test evidence are saved beside this review.
